title: Monday Night Football
novel:
It was [[Super Bowl|Super Bowl]] Sunday, and the gang had a [[tradition|tradition]] — they all watched the game together at MacLaren's. But this year, everyone had other [[plans|plan]]. Robin had to [[work|work]] the late [[shift|shift]]. Marshall and Lily had a [[couples|couple]] [[therapy|therapy]] [[session|session]]. Barney had a [[date|date]] he could not [[cancel|cancel]].

"This is the first time in seven years we're not watching together!" Ted [[complained|complain]]. He decided to [[record|record]] the game and watch it alone the next day, [[avoiding|avoid]] all [[spoilers|spoiler]] for twenty-four hours.

This was nearly [[impossible|impossible]] in New York. Everywhere Ted went, people were [[screaming|scream]] about the game. He walked past a [[sports|sport]] bar and had to [[physically|physical]] [[plug|plug]] his ears. A [[stranger|strange]] on the [[subway|subway]] started to tell him the score and Ted literally ran away.

But when he finally sat down to watch the recorded game, he felt [[lonely|lonely]]. The [[excitement|excite]] was not just about the game — it was about being together. The [[cheering|cheer]], the [[arguments|argument]] about which team was better, Barney's [[ridiculous|ridiculous]] [[bets|bet]] — that was the point.

One by one, his friends [[appeared|appear]] at the door. Robin had [[swapped|swap]] her shift. Marshall and Lily had [[rescheduled|reschedule]] therapy. Even Barney had [[dumped|dump]] his date. "We couldn't let you watch alone," Lily said.

They watched the game together — a day late, but exactly right.
